main_body: Three stacked vertical wooden posts on the right, each with a light end-grain top and a brown front, beside a left strip of light-orange vertical planks on a dark background. It is a tileable strip rather than one frame.
top_band: Light tan end-grain square with a darker cross centre, about rows 2-7 of each 16-row segment. It reads as a post end rather than a wide horizontal surface.
evidence: Each post is a narrow vertical shaft with a small tan cap and a flat brown face below it. There are no horizontal beams or base with visible top faces, so it does not meet the frame requirement. No distinct front-edge line or eave shadow separates the cap from the face. The left plank strip is a flat vertical face. Rows 0-1 and 14-16 of each segment are grey blocks that read as flat caps or bases, not 3/4 surfaces.

style.evidence: The wood ramps have about 3-4 steps with some grain. The dark near-black background fills large flat areas, and the grey blocks are flat with 2-3 tones. Tiles carry few colours compared with the cheese stall and well references, which have many more shading steps, texture dots and detail. The piece looks thinner and flatter next to them.
